title: Meta Releases Muse Ember for Agent Execution Tasks
summary: Meta's Muse Ember launches as a lightweight AI model designed for agent workflows, tool calls, and parsing at 10 cents per million tokens.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Meta launched Muse Ember on November 9, 2026, as its lightest AI model optimized for agent execution and repetitive tasks.
- Priced at 10 cents per million tokens, Ember undercuts competitors like Anthropic Haiku and OpenAI Luna while maintaining high accuracy.
- Ember handles multimodal inputs including text, images, and audio, designed to pair with Muse Wonder in agentic workflows.


Meta Superintelligence Lab has officially launched Muse Ember, a new lightweight AI model designed specifically for agent execution workflows. Released on November 9, 2026, Ember represents Meta's most cost-efficient AI offering yet, targeting the repetitive tasks that define modern agentic systems: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, data extraction, and long document parsing.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially launched on November 9, 2026, Muse Ember arrives as the fourth model in Meta's Muse family. The release follows Spark in April, its open-source counterpart Glimmer in August, and the flagship Wonder model in October. Ember is immediately available for developers seeking cost-effective agent infrastructure.


## Pricing and Cost Efficiency


Ember's standout feature is its pricing structure. At 10 cents per million input tokens, the model significantly undercuts frontier competitors like Anthropic's Haiku and OpenAI's Luna. Meta highlighted this advantage using Artificial Analysis's composite benchmark, demonstrating that Ember delivers both lower costs and higher accuracy scores than comparable models.


The pricing also positions Ember competitively against open-source alternatives like DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM 5.3 Flash. This aggressive cost positioning signals Meta's intent to capture high-volume agent workloads where token costs accumulate rapidly across thousands or millions of daily operations.


## Agent Execution Architecture


Meta designed Ember to function as the execution layer in multi-model agentic systems. The recommended pattern pairs Ember with Muse Wonder, Meta's frontier reasoning model. In this configuration, Wonder handles strategic planning and rule establishment while Ember executes those rules at scale.


Consider a customer support scenario: Wonder might analyze incoming tickets to establish routing logic and response templates. Ember then applies those decisions across tens of thousands of support cases, handling the volume work while maintaining accuracy. As Meta frames it, "Muse Wonder plans, Muse Ember handles the volume."


## Multimodal Capabilities


Unlike many lightweight models restricted to text processing, Ember supports multiple input formats:


- Text processing for traditional document and code tasks
- Image understanding for screenshots, charts, and scanned documents
- Audio processing for voice memos and meeting recordings


This multimodal design eliminates the need for separate preprocessing models in agent pipelines. Developers can route diverse input types directly to Ember without format conversion steps, simplifying architecture and reducing latency.


## Position in Meta's AI Ecosystem


Ember completes a strategic product ladder for Meta. Spark serves mid-weight general tasks, Glimmer provides an open-source option for developers seeking model ownership, Wonder tackles frontier reasoning challenges, and Ember now occupies the high-throughput execution tier.


The timing aligns with the growing momentum of Meta's consumer-facing[Muse Agent](https://emergent.sh/news/meta-muse-openai-dots-ai-agents-launch-amid) , which launched in September and recently added features like[Spaces](https://emergent.sh/news/meta-muse-spaces-launch-collaborate-ai-agents) for collaborative work and[video chat](https://emergent.sh/news/meta-muse-voice-now-available-us-video-chat) capabilities. Ember provides the infrastructure for scaling those consumer experiences while managing compute costs.


## What This Means


Muse Ember fills a critical gap in the agent execution market where cost per task often determines viability at scale. By combining aggressive pricing with multimodal support and proven accuracy, Meta challenges both proprietary and open-source competitors in the lightweight model segment. For developers building production agent systems, Ember offers a credible alternative to more expensive frontier models for routine execution tasks. The strategic pairing with Wonder establishes a clear architectural pattern: heavier models for reasoning, lighter models for volume, a division that may define how enterprises structure their AI infrastructure in 2027 and beyond.
